citation: O'Brien, Mahon. "Being, Nothingness and Anxiety." In Heidegger on Affect, edited by Christos Hadjioannou, 1-28. Philosophers in Depth. Cham: Palgrave Macmillan, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-24639-6_1
thesis: Being and Time (1927) is continuous with, not superseded or discontinued by, Heidegger's later (1929, 1935, 1940s) treatments of Being and the Nothing; bare moods (Befindlichkeit/Stimmung), and above all anxiety (Angst) understood as a fundamental mood rather than a directed feeling, are phenomenal evidence -- already present in BT -- of Dasein's standing exposure to the interplay of presence and absence, in service of a fundamental ontology rather than psychology, anthropology, humanism, or existentialism. Chapter authored by Mahon O'Brien; Hadjioannou is the volume editor only (and separately authored a later chapter). Engages BT, 'What Is Metaphysics?' (1929/1943/1949) and Introduction to Metaphysics (1935, IM), not the 1929/30 Fundamental Concepts of Metaphysics (FCM) lecture course; boredom appears only once, in a quoted IM passage naming it alongside despair and joy.

sections.title: Being and Nothing -- Heidegger's own retrospective account of BT via the 1929 'What Is Metaphysics?' (PM), its 1943 postscript/1949 introduction, and the 1935 Introduction to Metaphysics (IM); Leibniz's founding question; the rejection of the principle of non-contradiction against Carnap; the chalk example (IM 32); Husserlian intentionality (lamp/picture/car) and 'Origin of the Work of Art' hearing-example (storm/plane/Mercedes)
Typographic section break marking the shift from historical-textual reconstruction to systematic argument

Why Moods? -- the IM 1-2 passage on despair/joy/boredom; return to BT's Befindlichkeit/Stimmung architecture (SZ section 29, 'prior to all psychology of moods'); anxiety (Angst) vs. fear (Furcht) via SZ section 40 and the 1929 lecture; throwness (Geworfenheit), falling (Verfallenheit)/turning-away as phenomenal evidence not counter-evidence; anxiety's object as 'nothing and nowhere within-the-world' (SZ 186-187); being-towards-death; closing citation to BT's stated aim of fundamental ontology (SZ 200)

Endnotes 1-15 -- Capobianco (n.1, the chapter's named discontinuist target), the Leibnizian question's phrasing (n.3), Dahlstrom (2010) on negation/negative facts quoted at length (nn.5, 8), Kaeufer (2001) on the historical context of Heidegger's engagement with logical positivism (n.7), Black Notebooks/GA 95 passages on disposition (n.13) and an explicit disavowal of 'philosophy of existence' (n.14)
Five entries: Capobianco (2010), Carnap (1932), Dahlstrom (2010), Heidegger (2017, Ponderings VII-XI), Kaeufer (2001)

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: single passing textual mention only, via the quoted IM 1-2 passage naming boredom alongside despair/joy; 'wasteland... makes no difference... whether beings are or are not' anticipates but is not FCM's own three-forms apparatus; not developed

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: same locus/quotation: 'the stubborn ordinariness of beings lays open a wasteland' -- a compact, pre-FCM statement of boredom-as-indifference, quoted not argued

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: not treated re: boredom specifically; analogical only (P/anticipatory-application) -- the chapter's own overarching concern is Dasein's ecstatic/finite temporality (having-been/not-yet, being-towards-death) as disclosed by anxiety, not boredom

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: not treated directly; adjacent only via Dasein's habitual absorption-in-things and 'turning-away' as evasion of anxiety, never applied to boredom or attention

readings.text: BT's reception was distorted from the outset by mutually incompatible misreadings (existentialism, nihilism, anthropology, psychology, humanism, subjectivism) that Heidegger 'bemoans... to the end of his life.'

Heidegger's 1940s retrospectives describe BT as already 'setting out on the way to prepare an overcoming of metaphysics'; any attempt to overcome metaphysics 'must continue to speak the language of that which they help overcome.'
Leibniz's question rests on the unexamined assumption that 'being' means continuous presence, so that 'the Nothing' can be dismissed as simpler and easier than any thing.

Ordinary talk of absence (a gap, nothing between hedges) shows 'being' is used of things not straightforwardly present; rewriting via existential quantifiers already presupposes being-as-presence, the very assumption in question.

The chalk example (IM 32): part of what it means for the chalk to be this chalk includes its possibility of being used up, a possibility belonging to the chalk itself, not added by thought; '∃xCx' cannot capture this possibility-dimension of being.

Heidegger rejects Carnap/logical positivism's invocation of the principle of non-contradiction to dismiss talk of 'the Nothing' as illogical; logic itself may rest on an unexamined prior decision about the meaning of being, not a 'gift from heaven.'

The traditional strategy of asking after the 'ground' of given beings (the vineyard-infestation analogy, IM 30) forecloses the more radical question by assuming beings are unquestionably given; the Nothing forces beings to be 'held out... into the possibility of not-Being.'

Husserlian intentionality (lamp, picture, passing car) shows ordinary perception already imaginatively 'fills out' what is not bare-presently given; Heidegger regarded this as one of Husserl's most important insights.

'Origin of the Work of Art' reinforces the point from hearing: we hear the storm, the plane overhead, and 'the Mercedes in immediate distinction from the Volkswagen' -- bare sensation is a derivative abstraction.

The IM 1-2 passage on despair/joy/boredom encodes, in miniature, Heidegger's abiding claim that bare moods are constant phenomenal evidence of Dasein's exposure to the interplay of presence and absence, not incidental psychic coloring.

The 'founding mode of attunement' both reveals beings as a whole and is itself 'the basic occurrence of our Da-sein'; bare moods are sharply distinguished from directed, thematic feelings caught up with worldly concerns.

Anxiety (Angst) is defined against fear (Furcht): fear is always fear of a particular threatening entity, whereas in anxiety 'all things that normally have significance are suddenly robbed of that same significance' and Dasein is anxious about, and before, nothing in particular.
Habitual absorption in things and 'turned-awayness' from anxiety is not counter-evidence against the phenomenal reality of the Nothing it discloses -- it is itself phenomenological testament to it.

BT already 'carefully laid the groundwork' for everything the later texts say: Dasein's basic state-of-mind is 'always in some kind of bare mood' (SZ 131-134), continuous with, not superseded by, 1929/1935/1940s developments.

Moods are explicitly not a contribution to psychology or anthropology: Heidegger's aim is 'one of fundamental ontology,' and moods must be seen 'prior to all psychology... as a fundamental existentiale.'

Much Heidegger misreading -- including the standard misreading of authenticity -- stems from failing to see that BT's investigation of Dasein is never a 'Dasein-oriented story' but always serves the meaning of Being in general.
Throwness (Geworfenheit) names the 'that it is' of Dasein's being delivered over to its 'there,' veiled in its whence/whither yet 'disclosed in itself all the more unveiledly.'
Fallenness/turning-away is not evidence against the phenomenal facts disclosed in mood but evidence for them: 'in the evasion itself the "there" is something disclosed.'

Anxiety's falling/turning-away is not grounded in fear of worldly entities; rather this turning-away is 'grounded... in anxiety', which in turn is what first makes fear possible at all -- anxiety is ontologically prior to fear.

That in the face of which one has anxiety is 'nothing and nowhere within-the-world': entities become so insignificant that the world's worldhood alone obtrudes -- it is, in short, 'the possibility of the ready-to-hand in general,' the world itself.

Being-towards-death and the constant 'passing away'/'moving towards' of finite existence are the temporal correlate of the anxiety analysis: Dasein is never purely present, always thrown, oriented toward its ultimate possibility of no-longer-being.

Closing citation: the analytic of Dasein is not meant to ground an anthropology, but rather 'its purpose is one of fundamental ontology' (SZ 200) -- confirming, in O'Brien's reading, that the whole 1927-1940s trajectory was never anything but this same project.

concepts.term: Leibniz's question (why beings rather than nothing)

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin
interlocutors.role: primary text under analysis across Being and Time (SZ), 'What Is Metaphysics?' and its 1943/1949 retrospectives (PM), Introduction to Metaphysics (IM, 1935), 'The Origin of the Work of Art' (BW), and the Black Notebooks (GA 95)

interlocutors.name: Capobianco, Richard
interlocutors.role: named discontinuist target: argues BT's textual difficulties require reading the later Heidegger as discontinuous with the earlier; O'Brien judges this 'a less than hermeneutically honest approach to a text'

interlocutors.name: Carnap, Rudolf
interlocutors.role: 1932 critique of Heidegger ('The Elimination of Metaphysics Through Logical Analysis of Language') targeted as the paradigm logical-positivist dismissal of talk about the Nothing as nonsense

interlocutors.name: Husserl, Edmund
interlocutors.role: source of 'intentionality,' which Heidegger regarded as one of Husserl's most important philosophical insights, used to show perception already outruns bare presence

interlocutors.name: Dahlstrom, Daniel
interlocutors.role: cited for 'Negation and Being' (2010) on negative facts and the perception of movement/change as involving an ineliminable negative moment; quoted at length in n.8. NOTE: also understood to be a contributor to this same edited volume (a later chapter, per this cluster's sibling units), though that chapter is not the work cited here and is not yet built in this cluster

interlocutors.name: Kaeufer, Stefan
interlocutors.role: cited (2001, 'On Heidegger on Logic') on the neo-Kantian backdrop to Heidegger's early engagement with logic, qualifying but not overturning O'Brien's reading of the 1929/1935 anti-positivist polemic

interlocutors.name: Leibniz, G.W.
interlocutors.role: source of the founding question ('why are there beings at all instead of nothing?') that structures the whole chapter

interlocutors.name: Macquarrie, John & Robinson, Edward
interlocutors.role: BT translators; their rendering of Befindlichkeit as 'state-of-mind' is defended by O'Brien as apt despite criticism in the literature

tensions.label: Continuity vs. discontinuity of early/late Heidegger
tensions.poles: O'Brien's own continuist reading (BT already anticipates 1929/1935/1940s developments) vs. Capobianco's discontinuist reading (BT's difficulties require treating later Heidegger as a break from the earlier)

tensions.label: Fundamental ontology vs. psychology/anthropology/existentialism/humanism
tensions.poles: Heidegger's own repeated insistence that BT's mood-analysis serves fundamental ontology alone vs. the field's persistent tendency to read BT's Angst/Befindlichkeit material as a contribution to psychology, philosophical anthropology, or existentialist humanism

tensions.label: Logic/non-contradiction vs. the meaningfulness of talk about the Nothing
tensions.poles: Carnap/logical-positivist dismissal of 'the Nothing' as illogical nonsense vs. Heidegger's claim that logic's own authority over the being-question is itself an unexamined, question-begging assumption
